help.title: Help & FAQ
help.desc: Answers to the questions people ask most.
help.intro: Anabasis is meant to be self-explanatory, but here are answers to the things people ask most. Still stuck? Send a note — we read every message.

faq.a: No. Anabasis works fully without signing up — open it and start logging straight away. An account is optional and only adds cross-device sync.

On your device, in your browser (IndexedDB). It works offline and never leaves your device unless you create a cloud account to sync. Clearing your browser's site data erases it, so export a backup first.
Yes. The full app is free and runs locally. There are no ads, no analytics and no third-party trackers.

faq.q: How do I install it on my phone?
faq.a: Open anabasis.axonos.dev in your browser, then use “Add to Home Screen” (the Share menu on iOS, the ⋮ menu on Android). It installs like a native app and works offline.
Create a free account and sign in on each device — your data then syncs automatically. Sync is last-write-wins per row and keeps working offline; changes sync when you reconnect.

faq.q: How do I back up or move my data?
faq.a: Settings → Data → Export writes a single JSON file with everything. Import reads it back on any device. This works with or without an account.

faq.q: Can I delete my account and data?
faq.a: Yes. Settings → Account → Delete account removes your cloud account and its synced rows from the server. Local data on a device is removed by clearing the browser's site data.

faq.q: Is it safe to follow the training?
faq.a: Anabasis is a tracker, not a coach or medical advice. Read the Safety & health notice, warm up, progress gradually and stop if something hurts. Train at your own risk.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: Anabasis is local-first. Your training data stays in your browser and is never sent anywhere unless you choose to create a cloud account for sync. There are no ads, no analytics and no third-party trackers.

sections.p: All your workouts, exercises, goals and body metrics are stored in your browser (IndexedDB). They work fully offline and never leave your device unless you enable cloud sync. Clearing your browser's site data deletes them — export a backup first.

sections.h: If you create a cloud account
sections.p: A cloud account stores your account email and your private sync rows on the Anabasis server so you can sync across devices. The server may keep short-lived technical logs (such as IP address and request metadata) to operate securely and rate-limit abuse. This data is used only to run the sync service — never sold or shared.

sections.h: No ads, no analytics, no trackers
sections.p: Anabasis runs no advertising, no analytics and no third-party tracking scripts, and sets no advertising cookies. We cannot see how you use the app.
Friends, ranking and the leaderboard are off by default. If you opt in, only aggregate figures (such as level and totals) are shared with friends — never your raw training data.

You can export all your data at any time from Settings → Data & backups. You can permanently delete your cloud account and its server-side rows from Settings → Account. Local data is removed by clearing the app's site data.
Questions about this policy can be raised on the project repository: github.com/Frezzaroukos/anabasis. Anabasis is a personal, non-commercial project by Aggelos Frezzaroukos.

safety.title: Safety notice
safety.intro: Anabasis is a training log, not medical or coaching advice. Strength training carries risk. Train sensibly and at your own risk.
safety.banner: Anabasis is a training log, not medical or coaching advice. Warm up, progress gradually, and stop if something hurts — you train at your own risk.

sections.p: Anabasis logs and structures training. It does not diagnose, treat or replace a doctor or coach. If you have a health condition, an injury, are pregnant, or feel pain or dizziness, consult a qualified professional before training.

Weighted calisthenics loads your joints, tendons and connective tissue, which adapt slower than muscle. Warm up properly, add weight in small steps, and master each progression before moving to the next.
Check your bar, rings, belt and anchors before loading them. Keep good form, and avoid training to failure on risky movements without a safe setup.
Sharp pain, joint pain or dizziness means stop. Rest and recover — progress comes from consistency over time, not from a single hard session.
